title: Make the webhook sender give way to a deploy

blocks.text: The notification service delivers webhooks to customers' endpoints from an outbox, on a pool that every deploy shuts down with `shutdownNow()`. Two complaints reached the team in the same week. Deploys wait for the notification pool until their timeout runs out. And during one deploy a customer's endpoint, which was down at the time, received a burst of identical requests within a few milliseconds.
`deliver(...)` already retries correctly. Finish the two `TODO`s in `src/main/java/practice/WebhookSender.java`:

items: `run()`: the sender's life on its pool thread;

blocks.text: When you're done, a deploy ends the sender whether it is waiting for the next payload or pausing before a retry, and no request goes to the endpoint after the deploy began. About ten lines in total.
The tests run the sender on a real `ExecutorService`. The pause they hand it doesn't wait, but it answers interrupts exactly as `Thread.sleep` does.

cases.says: a rejected payload is retried after growing pauses until it is accepted, and the payloads after it are delivered in order
once a deploy arrives during a pause, the endpoint is not called again for that payload
after a delivery gives up because of a deploy, the thread still shows that it was asked to stop
a sender waiting for its next payload ends when its pool is shut down

origin.section: Whoever Catches InterruptedException Rethrows It, or Restores It and Stops

concepts: Whoever catches InterruptedException rethrows it, or restores the flag and stops; an empty catch ignores the request and restoring then retrying turns every wait into a spin.
Wrapping InterruptedException in an unchecked exception makes a stop request look like an ordinary failure and loses the flag.
